problems.question:
Calculate the range of the following data set:
12, 15, 8, 21, 17, 9, 14

What is the range of this data set?
3, 8, 12, 5, 17, 9, 11, 6
For the data set: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, what is the median (Q2)?
problems.explanation: There are 7 values. The median is the 4th value in the sorted list: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28. The median is 16.

problems.question: A box plot shows minimum = 5, Q1 = 12, median = 18, Q3 = 25, maximum = 35. What is the range?

Find the lower quartile (Q1) of this data set:
6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30
problems.explanation: 9 values sorted. The median (Q2) is the 5th value = 18. Lower half (values below 18): 6, 9, 12, 15. Q1 is the median of these 4 = (9 + 12) ÷ 2 = 10.5

problems.question:
Calculate the interquartile range (IQR) for this data set:
10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34, 38, 42

The temperatures (°C) recorded over 12 days are:
15, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 30, 33

What is the interquartile range?
A data set has Q1 = 18, Q2 = 25, and Q3 = 34. What is the interquartile range?
A box plot shows minimum = 4, Q1 = 10, median = 16, Q3 = 25, maximum = 38. Which statement is true about the data?
options: 50% of the data lies between 10 and 25
25% of the data lies between 4 and 10
problems.explanation: Q1=10 and Q3=25, so the middle 50% of data is between 10 and 25. 25% of data lies below Q1=10. 75% of data lies below Q3=25. All three statements are correct.

problems.question:
The test scores of 15 students are:
32, 45, 47, 51, 53, 56, 58, 62, 65, 68, 72, 75, 79, 84, 91

What is the median score?
problems.explanation: 15 values. The median is the (15+1)/2 = 8th value when sorted. The 8th value is 62.

problems.question:
A data set of 10 values is:
2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 50

Using the 1.5 × IQR rule, is the value 50 an outlier?
options: Yes, because 50 exceeds the upper fence of 31
No, because 50 is less than the upper fence of 37
Yes, because 50 is greater than Q3
problems.explanation: 10 values. Sorted: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 50. Lower half (first 5): 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Q1 = 6. Upper half (last 5): 12, 14, 16, 18, 50. Q3 = 16. IQR = 16 − 6 = 10. Upper fence = Q3 + 1.5×IQR = 16 + 15 = 31. Since 50 > 31, the value 50 is an outlier.

problems.question:
The masses (kg) of 11 people are:
52, 55, 58, 60, 62, 64, 67, 70, 73, 78, 82

Using the 1.5 × IQR rule, are there any outliers?
problems.explanation: 11 values. Q1 is the 3rd value = 58. Q3 is the 9th value = 73. IQR = 73 − 58 = 15. Lower fence = Q1 − 1.5×IQR = 58 − 22.5 = 35.5. Upper fence = Q3 + 1.5×IQR = 73 + 22.5 = 95.5. All values lie between 35.5 and 95.5, so there are no outliers.

problems.question:
A group of 12 students recorded the number of text messages they sent in a day:
18, 22, 25, 28, 30, 34, 36, 40, 45, 48, 52, 80

Using the 1.5 × IQR rule, which value(s) would be classified as outliers?
A box plot has the following five-number summary: minimum = 10, Q1 = 20, median = 28, Q3 = 38, maximum = 55. What is the shape of the distribution?
problems.explanation: The right whisker (max − Q3 = 55 − 38 = 17) is longer than the left whisker (Q1 − min = 20 − 10 = 10). The median (28) is closer to Q1 (20) than to Q3 (38). Both indicate the data is positively skewed (skewed right).

problems.question:
The ages of 9 people are:
10, 12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 60

The value 60 is an outlier. What best describes its effect on the range compared to the IQR?
options: The range more than doubles while the IQR increases slightly
The range stays the same while the IQR increases
Both range and IQR more than double
The range is unaffected but the IQR increases significantly

problems.question:
A data set has 8 values. The sorted values are:
5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, 33

What are the values of Q1 and Q3?
problems.explanation: 8 values. Q1 is the median of the lower 4: 5, 9, 13, 17. Q1 = (9+13)/2 = 11. Q3 is the median of the upper 4: 21, 25, 29, 33. Q3 = (25+29)/2 = 27.
